item.description: Massive flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday killed at least 22 people and left hundreds of tourists, workers and others missing after sweeping through communities and bringing travel in parts of the Himalayan country to a halt. item.title: Pastoralists in a Changing World
item.description: Pastoralism is one of humanity’s oldest ways of life. Moving livestock across vast landscapes in rhythm with seasonal change and environmental conditions, pastoralist cultures rely on freedom of movement and shared arrangements over how to graze rangelands. Today, pastoralists are navigating profound environmental changes to the lands that have sustained their communities for generations. This […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Terremotos en Venezuela, Colombia e Indonesia: historias de mujeres que resisten
item.description: Los terremotos que sacudieron Venezuela, Colombia e Indonesia dejaron miles de personas damnificadas y comunidades enteras enfrentadas a la pérdida y la incertidumbre. Pero entre los escombros también emergen historias de resiliencia, solidaridad y cuidado. En esta edición especial de Ellas Hoy, nuestros periodistas viajaron a las zonas afectadas para contar cómo las mujeres sobrevivientes se aferran a lo que queda, sostienen a sus familias y lideran los esfuerzos de ayuda y reconstrucción. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Africa's herbarium collections are a scientific treasure. They need to be digitized before more biodiversity is lost
item.description: Universities and biodiversity institutes have hidden treasures: their collections of pressed plant specimens. These plants have been flattened, dried and mounted on special cardboard sheets. Some were collected centuries ago. They hold information about where species occur and how ecosystems have changed over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate change exposes up to 560 million children globally to at least one additional month of dangerous heat per year
item.description: New research by Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) shows that globally, up to 560 million children ages 0–9 (43% of all children in this age group) experience at least one additional month (30 or more days) of heat stress per year because of human-induced climate change. This exposure outpaces that of any other age group and is nearly triple the 190 million people (30%) ages 60–69 experiencing this additional health threat. Children are therefore already facing disproportionately high levels of dangerous humid heat caused by human-induced climate change, with exposure expected to grow under… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Buried underwear shows land use is key to soil health
item.description: Soil is the foundation of our food supply. It stores water, carbon and nutrients and is home to a large share of the world's biodiversity. More than half of global biodiversity is estimated to live below ground. Yet biodiversity, and with it soil health, is declining worldwide, with consequences for agriculture, food security and the functioning of entire ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Congo Basin study reveals nuanced relationship between people and flooding
item.description: In the Lac Télé Community Reserve, a vast tropical peatland in Africa's Congo Basin that is home to about 20,000 people, the forces of climate change and globalization are hitting residents hard. The seasonal floods upon which village communities have long relied are arriving earlier, staying longer and pushing farther into places that used to remain dry. And these impacts vary dramatically from one village to the next, a new Yale-led study finds. Fuente: Phys.org.
